the direct presidential veto is established by BATCH-0047-E013, while broader appointment obstruction requires actor-by-actor attribution.","BATCH-0021-R02-E001 supports CNDH investigation and partial SEDENA/UEILCA cooperation, but not “continuing GIEI/CNDH involvement” as a single favorable proposition; the GIEI left in 2023, and the CNDH account concerns its own subsequent work.","Surviving courts and civil-society activity show that scrutiny remained possible, but BATCH-0026-E017 concerns electoral Plan B rather than investigation of López Obrador’s conduct or associates, so it is only indirect contrary evidence for this lens."],"material_omissions":["Omits BATCH-0004-E020, which directly documents military concealment in the 2023 Dirty War inquiry despite a presidential access decree.","Omits BATCH-0004-E008 and BATCH-0003-E005/E011 concerning the disappearance-registry recount, leadership resignation, closure of the National Human Identification Center, alleged data manipulation, and access-to-information consequences.","Omits BATCH-0010-E001, BATCH-0030-E012, and BATCH-0031-E014 concerning the response to surveillance of Encinas, Pegasus surveillance of victim representatives, and presidential backing of military noncooperation.","Omits the broader appointment and capacity record in BATCH-0018-E015, BATCH-0026-E014, BATCH-0026-E004, and BATCH-0016-E010, including vacancies, court-compelled appointments, and prosecutorial staffing and funding reductions.","Does not cover investigations of family conflicts and associates reflected in BATCH-0005-E003/E004, BATCH-0008-E004, and BATCH-0046-E008, even though the question expressly includes assets, campaigns, and associates."]},{"question_id":"7B.7","factual_support_1_to_5":4,"completeness_1_to_5":2,"balance_1_to_5":4,"attribution_and_period_1_to_5":3,"judge_usefulness_1_to_5":3,"material_errors":["The conclusion of “documented presidential obstruction” is stronger than the Ayotzinapa passages alone establish. Those passages document a presidential order, military noncompliance, presidential defense of the military, and failure to compel compliance; direct obstruction by López Obrador is better established for the INAI veto and repeated secrecy order.","The journalist-disclosure paragraph combines conduct from different periods. BATCH-0031-E010 includes Loret de Mola’s 2022 disclosure and a later disclosure of Natalie Kitroeff’s telephone number; it should not present the whole pattern as 2023 conduct without dating each episode.","BATCH-0026-E020 is placed in the contrary list even though its main INAI facts—paralysis and support for dissolution—are adverse; only the later Supreme Court restoration is qualifying.","BATCH-0004-E012’s broad statement that government generally took credible enforcement steps is country-level and cannot establish López Obrador’s personal compliance with accountability duties."],"material_omissions":["Omits BATCH-0031-E013, which reports failure to implement the Supreme Court’s 2023 National Guard ruling and a renewed legislative effort to preserve military control—highly relevant judgment-compliance evidence.","Omits BATCH-0004-E008 and BATCH-0003-E011 on the missing-person registry revision and alleged manipulation, a central concealment theme.","Omits BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0010-E001, and BATCH-0047-E007 on inconsistent official treatment of Pegasus evidence and lack of corrective investigation.","Omits BATCH-0010-E011 and BATCH-0009-E011 on information denials, national-security classifications, INAI funding, and appointment obstruction.","Omits BATCH-0004-E020 and BATCH-0030-E012 on military obstruction of the Dirty War and Ayotzinapa inquiries.","Provides almost no coverage of audits, subpoenas, pardons, or disclosure duties beyond INAI, despite acknowledging that gap; the full index contains audit and procurement-transparency evidence relevant to disclosure and concealment."]},{"question_id":"7B.8","factual_support_1_to_5":4,"completeness_1_to_5":2,"balance_1_to_5":4,"attribution_and_period_1_to_5":3,"judge_usefulness_1_to_5":3,"material_errors":["The answer calls the Ayotzinapa record a “later retreat from earlier support.” The cited record supports vanished support and failure to compel military cooperation, but it does not establish a formal reversal of the original investigative commitment.","The statement that reported Pegasus surveillance conflicted with López Obrador’s promise is supported, but the cited surveillance largely occurred in 2019–2022; the answer should distinguish 2023 revelation and response from target-year implementation.","Banxico’s continued independence and court resistance are not evidence that López Obrador kept commitments; they show that institutions resisted or corrected his conduct. The answer recognizes this but still presents them as countervailing evidence to his good faith.","No cited evidence establishes that the identified reversals or secrecy measures were undertaken “for personal advantage,” an express part of the lens. The answer notes missing financial advantage but still reaches a materially adverse holistic characterization without clearly separating ordinary policy reversal from integrity-weighted opportunism."],"material_omissions":["Omits BATCH-0055-E007 and BATCH-0031-E013 concerning the stated civilian character of the National Guard reform versus its legal transfer of control to Defense and the response after the Supreme Court invalidated it.","Omits BATCH-0042-E009, BATCH-0043-E009, BATCH-0026-E002, and BATCH-0046-E004, which provide broader promise and factual-claim records, albeit with period and source limitations.","Omits BATCH-0013-E015 and BATCH-0026-E022 on major policy commitments, implementation reversals, and retrospective assessments of inconsistent statements.","Omits BATCH-0016-E003 on security and social-program commitments and the allegation of clientelistic implementation.","Omits BATCH-0026-E010 and BATCH-0018-E010 concerning commitments and conduct affecting elections, journalists, and legal protections.","Does not systematically distinguish broken outcome promises from bad-faith commitments, concealed tradeoffs, honest policy change, or institutional incapacity—the core analytical boundary of this lens."]},{"question_id":"7B.9","factual_support_1_to_5":4,"completeness_1_to_5":2,"balance_1_to_5":4,"attribution_and_period_1_to_5":4,"judge_usefulness_1_to_5":3,"material_errors":["BATCH-0008-E007 is a secondary summary alleging contracts to friends of López Obrador’s son; it does not establish that the son distributed the contracts or that López Obrador knowingly tolerated the procurement scheme. The answer appropriately qualifies the ultimate conclusion but initially describes the contract pattern too compactly.","The closure of the Pío investigation is not straightforwardly contrary evidence of avoidance of favoritism: the decision remained subject to judicial confirmation, followed a long period without progress, and does not establish independent or effective accountability.","Recovery action against García Luna under a prior administration is weak contrary evidence for favoritism toward López Obrador’s own family and network.","The asserted pattern of “personal attribution ... for knowledge, public defense, and tolerance” overstates tolerance. Public defense and knowledge of allegations are documented; knowing tolerance of proven favoritism is not established because the underlying wrongdoing and adequacy of the ordered review remained unresolved."],"material_omissions":["Omits detailed family and network evidence in BATCH-0005-E004, including the 2019 family-business memorandum, contracts involving a cousin, purchases directed to a son’s friend, and appointments of allegedly inexperienced loyalists.","Omits BATCH-0040-E004 and BATCH-0009-E008 concerning family-and-friend appointments and alleged political influence.","Omits BATCH-0048-E012 and BATCH-0029-E007 on military privileged access to contracts, revenue streams, infrastructure, and reduced transparency, while carefully requiring proof of López Obrador’s direction or knowing tolerance.","Omits BATCH-0016-E003 and BATCH-0031-E015 concerning alleged clientelistic design or distributional effects of social programs; these are not decisive without stronger proof but belong in a full-index assessment.","Omits BATCH-0028-E006 and BATCH-0046-E008 on López Obrador’s appointment and later reassignment of longtime associate Ignacio Ovalle after the Segalmex scandal.","Does not address licensing, pardons, or enforcement favoritism, and gives only a narrow procurement treatment despite the full index containing broader privileged-access and selective-enforcement allegations."]},{"question_id":"7B.10","factual_support_1_to_5":3,"completeness_1_to_5":2,"balance_1_to_5":4,"attribution_and_period_1_to_5":3,"judge_usefulness_1_to_5":3,"material_errors":["The answer cites BATCH-0047-E013 and BATCH-0029-E006/BATCH-0047-E008 in the prose but omits the former from both evidence-ID lists and classifies the press-attack items only as “contrary or qualifying,” even though they are central adverse support for its conclusion. The structured evidence lists therefore do not faithfully represent the answer.","The favorable claim that the administration “operated some corruption-enforcement processes” relies largely on governmental or country-level actions and is not strong evidence of López Obrador’s personal ethical example.","BATCH-0015-E016 and BATCH-0015-E018 concern broad UN-government initiatives, including many subnational or UN-led actions, and offer little direct support for López Obrador’s personal ethical example.","BATCH-0021-R01-E010 shows activity by an autonomous body, much of it involving state authorities; it is evidence that checks survived, not that López Obrador supported durable integrity institutions.","The opening description “mixed but predominantly adverse” is plausible for the selected evidence but insufficiently grounded in the full integrity index because truthfulness, conflicts, family benefit, appointments, and favoritism evidence is largely omitted."],"material_omissions":["Omits extensive direct truthfulness and correction evidence, including BATCH-0042-E009, BATCH-0043-E009, BATCH-0026-E016/E022, and BATCH-0009-E012.","Omits the family-conflict, favoritism, and self-dealing themes in BATCH-0005-E004, BATCH-0008-E011, BATCH-0026-E003, BATCH-0046-E008, and related entries, despite their direct relevance to ethical example and impunity.","Omits broader evidence about attacks on the press and integrity critics in BATCH-0007-E005, BATCH-0012-E009, BATCH-0018-E002/E003, BATCH-0044-E012, and BATCH-0046-E010.","Omits evidence concerning alleged politicized anti-corruption enforcement and weakening of autonomous institutions in BATCH-0003-E019, BATCH-0013-E014, BATCH-0026-E004, and BATCH-0016-E021/E022.","Omits available public-trust and ethical-norm context, including International IDEA and retrospective AP assessments, while correctly noting that direct causal measurement of public trust is absent.","The answer does not synthesize the repeated family-defense, institutional-impunity, and selective-enforcement evidence that a skeptical judge would need to evaluate whether adverse conduct was isolated or normalized."]}],"verdict":"fail","strengths":["All five answers generally distinguish personal presidential conduct from military, legislative, autonomous-body, subnational, and inherited conduct.","They repeatedly distinguish allegations and evaluative reporting from final judicial findings.","They acknowledge target-year limitations and avoid inferring personal financial benefit or intent where the cited passages do not establish it.","They include meaningful contrary evidence and avoid claiming total institutional capture."],"systemic_problems":["The answers do not assess the full candidate index. Each relies on a narrow recurring set of Ayotzinapa, INAI, Pegasus, and press-freedom items while omitting numerous directly indexed candidates.","Structured supporting and contrary evidence lists are inconsistent with the prose and sometimes reverse polarity; several decisive adverse citations appear only in the contrary list or in neither list.","Institutional survival or court resistance is repeatedly used as favorable balance even when it was not supported or voluntarily accepted by López Obrador.","Country-level enforcement and UN-cooperation evidence is sometimes treated as favorable personal-integrity evidence despite weak ruler attribution.","Period handling is usually caveated but not consistently applied: 2022 conduct, 2024 retrospectives, and later disclosures are sometimes blended into a 2023 conclusion.","The answers identify major gaps in their own “reopen” fields but still state relatively confident directional conclusions instead of clearly limiting those conclusions to the covered themes."],"concrete_corrections_required":["Rebuild each answer against every candidate indexed to its question, recording inclusion, exclusion, duplication, period fit, attribution, and evidentiary weight.","Correct the evidence-ID arrays so every material prose citation appears in the appropriate supporting or qualifying list, with adverse evidence supporting an adverse conclusion classified consistently.","For 7B.6 and 7B.7, add the Dirty War inquiry, disappearance-registry changes, surveillance remedies, prosecutorial capacity, broader appointment record, and National Guard judgment-compliance evidence.","For 7B.8, distinguish unfulfilled outcomes from proved bad faith and analyze the National Guard reversal, broader promise record, and absence of demonstrated personal advantage.","For 7B.9, add the full family, associate, loyalist-appointment, military-access, social-program, and Segalmex/Ovalle record while preserving allegation-versus-finding limits.","For 7B.10, incorporate truthfulness, correction, family conflicts, selective enforcement, favoritism, appointments, and durable-institution evidence rather than basing the ethical-example conclusion mainly on scrutiny and press treatment.","Date every material episode explicitly and separate conduct occurring in 2023 from earlier conduct, 2023 disclosure of earlier conduct, and post-2023 retrospective reporting.","Treat independent court, media, CNDH, and civil-society resistance as evidence of surviving checks, not affirmative ruler integrity, unless the record shows presidential acceptance, support, compliance, or correction."],"safe_for_judge_use":false,"rationale":"The answers are cautious and often factually well qualified, but they fail the requested full-index evaluation standard. Material omissions span every lens, and evidence polarity, ruler attribution, and period classification are not consistently reflected in the structured fields. A judge could use these as thematic summaries of selected evidence, but not as reliable comprehensive lens analyses without substantial correction."}
